title: test_shim_starts_the_loop names on a box without systemd that it cannot run there, and exits non-zero, instead of four FileNotFoundError tracebacks
intention: On a platform without systemctl or /proc, test_shim_starts_the_loop.py prints ONE named line saying it needs systemd user units and /proc and cannot run there, and exits non-zero before any tooth runs, instead of every tooth dying with a FileNotFoundError traceback. That is an honest red at a diagnostic surface (Law 7); the sealer is Linux (outline 9.4.2.3.3.1). On Linux it is unchanged. When the NOTRUN mechanism (ticket for the tester and proof_coverage) lands, a follow-up turns the line into NOTRUN.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell, house checkout and a worktree alike: test_shim_starts_the_loop.py reds 4 teeth with 'FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]' (test_a_held_lock_spawns_nothing, test_dead_to_live_one_shim, test_two_shims_one_loop, test_the_setsid_path_leaves_no_scratch_process). The proof's own helpers call `systemctl --user` (lines 107-112, 203) and scan /proc (lines 131-134, 215, 326), and the setsid tooth builds a PATH dir of linux tools (line 289). It is Linux-only by construction. A skip that exits 0 is impossible: the tester reads exit 0 with no green tooth as RED (device.py:736-745), and the NOTRUN state outline 9.4.8.1 describes is not built. The orchestrator ruled this interim: one named line, a non-zero exit, no tracebacks. No ticket owned the Windows red.
traces_to: Law 7 (an error is loud at a diagnostic surface, named), Law 3 and Law 9 (red is the default; no skip dressed as green), and outline 9.4.2.3.3.1 (one sealer, on cairn's home, Linux).
how: At the top of main(), if systemctl is not found on PATH or /proc does not exist, print one line: 'test_shim_starts_the_loop: needs systemd user units and /proc, which this box lacks (<platform>); the Linux sealer measures it (outline 9.4.2.3.3.1)', and return a non-zero status before any tooth runs. Do not touch the teeth. Linux behaviour is unchanged.

clauses.claim: on a platform with no systemctl or no /proc the proof prints one line naming that it needs systemd user units and /proc, and exits non-zero before any tooth runs, with no FileNotFoundError traceback, where on Windows it died with it in four teeth
on Linux the platform check is inert and the proof runs every tooth exactly as before

decisions.text: D1: a platform preamble in main(): one named line and a non-zero exit when systemctl or /proc is absent; the teeth are untouched.

out: cairn/tools/base/shim.py (the product is not at fault)
the NOTRUN mechanism (its own ticket against the tester and proof_coverage)

measured.saw: bin/cairn test of test_shim_starts_the_loop.py on Windows: 4 FAIL lines, all 'FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2]', in the untouched house checkout and in a worktree. Linux-only calls: subprocess.run(['systemctl', ...]) at lines 107, 108, 112, 203; Path('/proc').iterdir() at lines 134, 215, 326; a PATH dir of linux tools at line 289. cairn/devices/tester/device.py:736-745 turns exit 0 with no named green tooth into RED, so a Windows no-op cannot be green; a NOTRUN marker is read by nothing (grep of tester, proof_coverage, validation_store, codemother).
measured.how: bin/cairn test over the file on Windows; grep -n over the file; read device.py 726-745; grep for not-run in non-proof code
